s.g: (biochemistry) A polysaccharide, consisting of xylose residues, found in the cell walls of some algae and plants.
(biochemistry) Any of various enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of xylan.
(pharmacology) A potent α₂-adrenergic agonist used for sedation, anesthesia, and analgesia in large nonhuman mammals, and as an adulterant in street drugs.
(botany) A vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of water and minerals taken up by the roots; also the primary component of wood.
(chemistry) Any of a group of three isomeric aromatic hydrocarbons, found in coal and wood tar.
(chemistry) A pentahydric alcohol, C₅H₁₂O₅, penta-hydroxy pentane; derived from xylose; used as a sweetener.

(music) Any musical instrument (percussion idiophone) made of wooden slats graduated so as to make the sounds of the scale when struck with a small drumstick-like mallet; the standard Western concert xylophone or one of its derivatives.
s.x: All I know how to play on my xylophone is "Mary Had a Little Lamb". Would you like to hear it?

s.g: To play a xylophone or to play something else as though it was a xylophone.
To move above a ridged surface or series of surfaces so as to hit every ridge, in a manner similar to playing quickly and sequentially on a xylophone.

xylophones.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of xylophone

s.g: (biochemistry) One of the pentoses, C₅H₁₀O₅, a white crystalline sugar, derived from wood.
The color space of the tristimulus values X, Y, and Z.
A generic placeholder representing a specific name or thing.

s.x: Person X, Person Y, Person Z

s.g: (web design, cartography) Describing a URL scheme for providing map tiles, where X and Y refer to coordinates, while Z refers to zoom level.
